title: The ten plagues (Exodus 7–10)
hookLine: blood, frogs, lice, swarms, pestilence, boils, hail, locusts, darkness
carry: ten ways to say let go

cards: At a Passover seder, there's a moment when someone reads out a list. At each word, people at many tables dip a finger in their wine and let a drop fall onto a plate. Blood.
Locusts. Darkness. The death of the firstborn.

teach.b: The Hebrew word is makot: blows, strikes. The Torah also calls them signs and wonders. They come in a rhythm.
Moses warns Pharaoh; Pharaoh refuses; the blow falls; Pharaoh begs and promises, and when it lifts, changes his mind. Again and again.
They start with the Nile, Egypt's lifeline, and the river where Hebrew babies were thrown. It turns to blood. Then frogs come up out of it, into bedrooms and ovens and kneading bowls.

teach.h: THIS IS THE FINGER OF GOD.
teach.b: At the third plague, Pharaoh's own magicians, who copied the first two, give up: "This is the finger of God."
Then swarms of wild creatures, and something new begins: the land of Goshen, where the Israelites lived, is set apart; the plague doesn't touch it.
Then pestilence on the livestock, boils, hail with fire running through it, locusts that eat everything the hail left. Then darkness, so thick that "they saw not one another" for three days.
But the Israelites, the text says, had light where they lived. Why so many? The Torah gives more than one reason.
On the last night, God says, "against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments."

teach.h: TEN WAYS TO SAY LET GO.
teach.b: Some readers match the plagues to powers Egypt held divine, like the Nile and the sun. Some rabbis added another reading: every plague was a chance for Pharaoh to change. Ten warnings, the same message louder each time.

how: At the Passover seder, as the ten plagues are read, many Jews remove a drop of wine from their cup for each one, and recite Rabbi Judah's three-word memory code.

o: sores: the painful boils of the sixth plague
blows or strikes: the ten plagues on Egypt
songs: the hymns sung beside the sea

games.q: what's inside the plagues — tap the pairs.
p: this is the finger of God

s: Pharaoh's magicians could copy every plague
they copied the first two, then said: this is the finger of God.
during the darkness, the Israelites had light
the text says they had light in their dwellings.
Rabbi Judah made a memory code for the plagues
detzach, adash, be'achav: the first letters of the ten.

games.q: you're one of Pharaoh's magicians. you matched the blood and the frogs. now lice rise from the dust, and you can't copy it. what do you tell Pharaoh?
o: this is the finger of God.
games.why: they tell him, "This is the finger of God." and Pharaoh still won't listen.

practice: The seder says every generation should see itself as if it had gone out of Egypt.
So name one thing that holds people in a narrow place now, for someone else or for yourself: debt, addiction, loneliness, injustice, fear, a phone that won't let go.
You don't have to fix it; just see it clearly, the way you'd see a plague.

wordCard.voice: Makot. Blows, strikes, plagues. The ten blows on Egypt, each one saying the same thing: let my people go.

orig.note: Hebrew: blows, strikes. the usual Jewish name for the ten plagues.

carryVoice: Your line: ten ways to say let go. Each blow came with a warning first. Day eighty-five, done.
